subject.title: fix(mcp): avoid memory spikes from oversized client TLS files

question: Should MCP client certificate and key files become unsupported above 64 KiB, or should the bounded reader use a more conservative compatibility limit?
rationale: The implementation mechanism is sound, but choosing the maximum supported certificate-chain and key size changes shipped MCP configuration behavior and cannot be inferred from the memory-safety goal alone.

options.title: Prove and document 64 KiB
options.body: Keep the proposed ceiling after adding realistic certificate-chain coverage near the limit and documenting the new upgrade failure boundary.

options.title: Raise the bounded ceiling
options.body: Choose a larger fixed maximum that still prevents mistaken multi-megabyte reads while reducing compatibility risk for enterprise certificate chains and keys.

options.title: Pause for a TLS size policy
options.body: Hold the PR until the MCP transport owner defines the supported certificate-chain and private-key size contract.

recommendation.title: Prove and document 64 KiB
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed ceiling after adding realistic certificate-chain coverage near the limit and documenting the new upgrade failure boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged remote MCP transport work introduced the configuration and runtime path whose supported TLS input contract is changing.
